title_en: Hunan Yahua Seed Industry Research Institute v. Zhang Yang — dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights
keywords_en: civil; dispute over infringement of new plant variety rights; first instance; intermediate people's court; Hunan Province; Jiangxi Province; Hainan Province; legal person; natural person; Seed Law; Regulations on the Protection of New Varieties of Plants; determination of repeated use of propagating material of an authorized variety; allocation of burden of proof for infringement; farmer's defense of self-propagation and self-use; new plant variety rights; rice breeding; production of infringing seeds; intellectual property; Zhang Yang infringement of new plant variety rights dispute
full_text_en:
湖南亚华种业研究院诉张杨侵害植物新品种权纠纷案

### [Case Summary]

Where a party, without authorization, uses the propagating material of an authorized variety repeatedly for producing the propagating material of another variety, and where the accused infringing seeds are genetically related to the authorized variety, the burden of proof regarding the fact that the authorized variety was used as the female parent to produce the accused infringing seeds shall be borne by the infringing party. In the accused infringing act, "repeated use" shall be understood as the act of repeatedly using the propagating material of the authorized variety as a parent stock to propagate separately with other parent stocks.

Plaintiff: Hunan Yahua Seed Science Research Institute, domiciled at Heping Road, Furong District, Changsha City, Hunan Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Yuanzhu, President of the Institute.

Defendant: Zhang Yang, male, born March 30, 1983, Han Chinese, residing in Paishang Town, Xiangdong District, Pingxiang City, Jiangxi Province.

Plaintiff Hunan Yahua Seed Science Research Institute (hereinafter referred to as Yahua Institute) filed a lawsuit with the Hainan Free Trade Port Intellectual Property Court against Defendant Zhang Yang for a dispute over infringement of a new plant variety right.

Plaintiff's Allegations: Yahua Institute is the variety rights holder of rice variety "Longke 638S" with variety right number CNA20090950.7, with a protection period of 15 years commencing March 1, 2014, which is still in effect. In May 2020, Yahua Institute discovered infringing activities involving large-scale breeding using "Longke 638S" rice in Sanya and commissioned Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. to file a complaint with the Sanya Municipal Agricultural and Rural Bureau and the Sanya Municipal Administrative Comprehensive Enforcement Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the Sanya Enforcement Bureau). Upon investigation by the administrative authority, it was found that Defendant Zhang Yang had produced 439 bags of the accused infringing seeds, totaling 35,120 jin. The Hangzhou Sub-Center of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs' New Plant Variety Testing Center identified the seeds in question, confirming the infringement by Zhang Yang. During the identification period, Zhang Yang transported all the accused infringing seeds to Pingxiang City, Jiangxi Province. The Pingxiang Municipal Agricultural Comprehensive Enforcement Detachment investigated Zhang Yang's infringing activities and found a portion of the accused infringing seeds at a factory building in Xiyuan Village, Xiabu Town, Xiangdong District, Pingxiang City, Jiangxi Province. After Yahua Institute obtained the variety right in question, it was licensed to its founder, Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd., and its affiliate Sichuan Longping High-Tech Seed Co., Ltd. for breeding and sales. The "Liangyou 1377" seeds bred using "Longke 638S" have an average market sales price of approximately RMB 33/jin and a breeding cost of approximately RMB 11/jin. Zhang Yang's unauthorized use of "Longke 638S" to breed 35,120 jin of "Liangyou 1377" seeds caused losses of approximately RMB 770,000. Pursuant to Articles 28 and 73 of the Seed Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Seed Law), Articles 6 and 39 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of New Plant Varieties (hereinafter referred to as the Plant Variety Protection Regulations), and Articles 2 and 6 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights, Zhang Yang's unauthorized use of "Longke 638S" for propagation and seed production constitutes an infringement of Yahua Institute's new plant variety right for rice "Longke 638S" (No. CNA20090950.7). Requests: 1. Zhang Yang immediately cease the infringement of the new plant variety right, destroy all infringing seed products and all female parent "Longke 638S" seeds he propagated; 2. Order Zhang Yang to pay RMB 500,000 in economic damages (including RMB 35,000 in reasonable expenses for rights protection).

Defendant's Defense: In early December 2019, Zhang Yang purchased over 100 jin of parent seeds from a non-party at a price of RMB 50/jin and planted them in Yazhou District, Sanya. On May 29, 2020, while drying the seeds, staff of the Sanya Enforcement Bureau inquired about the source, planting area, total yield, and purpose of the rice seeds, and notified Zhang Yang to transport the seeds back to his hometown in Jiangxi, with a prohibition on sale or sowing within seven days. At the time of the inquiry, employees of Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. were also present, stating that they would contact Zhang Yang within a month to handle these rice seeds. Zhang Yang transported the seeds to Xiabu Town, Xiangdong District, Pingxiang City, Jiangxi Province. After further drying, removing stalks, winnowing, and other selection processes for two to three days, and repackaging, there were about 280 bags of seeds meeting the requirements. Lacking funds to rent a suitable warehouse for seed storage, Zhang Yang stored the seeds in an abandoned factory building. On June 22, 2020, staff of the Pingxiang Municipal Agricultural and Rural Bureau found Zhang Yang and photographed the seeds in question, instructing him to keep them onsite. However, after four to five months, no one came to handle the seeds. Due to heavy rainfall and high humidity in Pingxiang during summer and autumn, coupled with severe roof leakage in the abandoned factory, by December 2020, most of the seeds had sprouted due to moisture and were no longer viable for planting or consumption. Zhang Yang was forced to feed the sprouted seeds to poultry. The weight of the seeds was not 35,120 jin; due to insufficient drying and lack of selection processes such as stalk removal and winnowing, they were not qualified seeds. After subsequent selection, the weight of the qualified seeds was approximately 26,000 jin, and Zhang Yang did not use them or sow them. Plaintiff Yahua Institute failed to provide sufficient evidence for the average sales price and breeding cost, and its claim for losses of approximately RMB 770,000 lacks evidentiary support. The seeds in question were not sold on the market or actually put into use, causing no loss to Yahua Institute. Zhang Yang had no subjective intent to infringe and should not bear liability for damages. Furthermore, Zhang Yang's breeding activity constituted self-propagation and self-use by a farmer without commercial purpose, using the propagating material of "Longke 638S" only once, which does not constitute repeated use. In summary, the claims of Yahua Institute lack factual basis and should be dismissed as a matter of law.

Facts Found by the Hainan Free Trade Port Intellectual Property Court at First Instance:

On December 25, 2009, Plaintiff Yahua Institute applied to the Ministry of Agriculture of the People's Republic of China for protection of the new plant variety "Longke 638S," and was granted authorization on March 1, 2014. The species or genus is rice, with variety right number CNA20090950.7 and a protection period of 15 years. Pursuant to Article 1 of the Notice of the Ministry of Finance and the National Development and Reform Commission on Cleaning Up and Standardizing the Policies Concerning Certain Administrative Fees (Cai Shui [2017] No. 20), as of April 1, 2017, fees for the protection of new plant varieties were abolished. On April 25, 2017, Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. paid the annual fee of RMB 1,000 for the fourth year of the variety right for "Longke 638S."

Plaintiff Yahua Institute submitted two major crop variety certification certificates, numbered 2017-1-0088 and 2018-1-0073, with variety name "Liangyou 1377," certification numbers Guoshen Dao 20176007 and Guishen Dao 2018075, and certification dates June 2017 and May 2018, respectively. These certificates show that the variety source of "Liangyou 1377" is "Longke 638S" × "R1377," meaning that "Liangyou 1377" is a hybrid rice variety bred by combining the female parent "Longke 638S" and the male parent "R1377." The two certificates also indicate that Yahua Institute is one of the breeders of "Liangyou 1377."

In May 2020, Plaintiff Yahua Institute discovered suspected infringing activities using "Longke 638S" rice for breeding at the drying yard of Haiyuan Company in Yazhou District, Sanya, and filed a complaint with the Sanya Municipal Agricultural and Rural Bureau and the Sanya Enforcement Bureau. On May 29 of the same year, law enforcement officers from the First Detachment of the Sanya Enforcement Bureau questioned Defendant Zhang Yang. When asked about the area and variety of hybrid rice he was breeding for southern propagation in Yazhou District, Sanya, Zhang Yang stated, "85 mu, it's Liangyou," "no agreement," "the parent seeds were introduced through an acquaintance in Sichuan and delivered door-to-door, cash only, at RMB 50 per jin," "I don't know what the parent seeds were, nor the name or phone number of the supplier," and that the seeds were "not for sale, only for my own contracted farmland use" and for planting "2,000 mu (requiring about 6 jin per mu)." At trial, Zhang Yang stated that he purchased the parent seeds from an unknown non-party, about 100 jin, and was unaware of the specific source, variety, or name of the seeds, estimating the yield as "439 bags (approximately 80 jin per bag), totaling 35,120 jin." Officers of the First Detachment of the Sanya Enforcement Bureau informed Zhang Yang that after transporting the seeds back to his hometown, he was not to sell or sow them. Subsequently, Zhang Yang transported all the seeds in question back to Jiangxi. On June 22 of the same year, the Pingxiang Municipal Agricultural Comprehensive Administrative Enforcement Detachment confirmed through on-site inspection that the seeds stored in the warehouse totaled 23,500 jin. Zhang Yang stated that after being questioned by the Sanya Enforcement Bureau, until December 2020, no one contacted him to handle the seeds. When the seeds became damp and sprouted, rendering them unusable for planting, he was forced to feed them to poultry.

On June 5, 2020, the Sanya Municipal Agricultural Comprehensive Enforcement Detachment commissioned the Hangzhou Sub-Center of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs' New Plant Variety Testing Center to test the sampled sealed paddy rice. The seal had signatures of Defendant Zhang Yang and other law enforcement officers across the seams. On June 15, 2020, the Center issued a *Crop Seed Quality Inspection Report* (Zhe) Zhong Zhong Jian Zi (2019) No. 01, which showed that the Center conducted authenticity testing on the submitted unknown variety sample against the control sample "Liangyou 1377" using the *Technical Procedure for Rice Variety Identification – SSR Marker Method*, comparing 48 locus points with 0 difference points, concluding "very similar variety or identical variety." On the same day, the Center issued an Identification Report stating that it performed identification on the submitted unknown variety sample against the control sample "Longke 638S" using SSR markers with reference to the standard *Technical Procedure for Rice Variety Identification – SSR Marker Method* (NY/T1433-2014) using capillary electrophoresis fluorescence detection. Twenty seeds were randomly selected, germinated, and mixed for DNA extraction, replicated twice. The result was: "Among the 48 SSR markers used, the unknown variety showed homozygous genotypes at 22 markers and heterozygous genotypes at the remaining 26 markers. The sample Longke 638S showed homozygous genotypes at all 48 markers, and one of its genotypes matched one genotype of the unknown variety." The conclusion stated: "The submitted sample and Longke 638S have a genetic relationship." Zhang Yang did not accept the authenticity, legality, or relevance of the above evidence, claiming he did not participate in the identification process and that the identification body lacked qualifications; he also did not accept the content of the report. The court found that in the transcript of the questioning by the First Detachment of the Sanya Enforcement Bureau, which was undisputed by Zhang Yang, there was a copy of the seed sample seal certificate (verified with the original) bearing Zhang Yang's signature. Zhang Yang's claim that he did not participate in the identification was contradictory, and he did not submit sufficient contrary evidence to rebut it. The Hangzhou Sub-Center of the Ministry of Agriculture's New Plant Variety Testing Center is a crop seed quality inspection institution announced in Announcement No. 2111 of the Ministry of Agriculture of the People's Republic of China on July 20, 2014, with the capacity to test the authenticity of major crop varieties including wheat and rice. Therefore, the court confirmed the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the Inspection Report and Identification Report submitted by Yahua Institute.

Plaintiff Yahua Institute is a non-governmentally funded institution established by Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd., and Sichuan Longping High-Tech Seed Co., Ltd. is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. On August 21, 2017, Yahua Institute signed a *Variety Rights Licensing Contract* with Sichuan Longping High-Tech Seed Co., Ltd., reaching an agreement on the licensing of new hybrid rice varieties including "Liangyou 1377" (female parent: Longke 638S × male parent: R1377), specifying that this variety is a hybrid rice variety submitted for approval by Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. and passed national certification (Guoshen Dao 20176007) in 2017. The *Liangyou Combination Seed Hainan Contract Production Contract* shows that Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. purchased "Liangyou 1377" seeds in Hainan at an average price of RMB 22/jin. The *Sichuan Longping 17-20 Liangyou 1377 Sales Table* shows that the average external sales price for "Liangyou 1377" was RMB 33/jin. The *Sichuan Longping Liangyou 1377 Recent Three-Year Sales Gross Profit Table* shows that the average annual net profit margin for Sichuan Longping High-Tech Seed Co., Ltd. in selling "Liangyou 1377" from 2017 to 2019 was 52%. Yahua Institute signed an *Entrusted Agency Contract* with Beijing Deheng (Changsha) Law Firm for this dispute, specifying legal fees of RMB 30,000 for rights protection activities, paid in full by Yuan Longping High-Tech Agriculture Co., Ltd. The transportation, accommodation, and meal expenses incurred by Yahua Institute for rights protection totaled RMB 5,000.

Regarding the evidence concerning the licensing of affiliated companies to produce and sell "Liangyou 1377" to infer profits, Defendant Zhang Yang did not dispute the authenticity and legality of some evidence but argued it was irrelevant to the case in dispute. He contended that the contracts and sales tables were documents issued by non-parties, prepared unilaterally by the non-parties, and could not be verified. Although he confirmed the authenticity and legality of the evidence for rights protection expenses, he argued that rights protection was not a necessary procedure and the expenses were not necessarily reasonable. The court determined that although the above evidence, interrelated, could prove the fact that Plaintiff Yahua Institute licensed its affiliates to use "Longke 638S" to produce and sell "Liangyou 1377" rice, the object of production and sale was "Liangyou 1377," which could not directly prove the value of "Longke 638S," for which variety protection was sought. Consequently, it was impossible to infer Yahua Institute's direct economic losses or Zhang Yang's profits from infringement. This evidence was not relevant and would not be used as evidence to determine the amount of damages in this case, only as a factor to be considered in the discretionary determination of damages. Yahua Institute claimed payment vouchers for reasonable rights protection expenses totaling RMB 35,000, including car rental fees, airfare, vehicle toll invoices, and legal fees, which are necessary expenses incurred for rights protection. The court accepted this.

Also found: Defendant Zhang Yang is a rural subsistence allowance recipient and holds a *Disability Certificate of the People's Republic of China* indicating a disability level and category of Class III physical disability.

Opinion of the Hainan Free Trade Port Intellectual Property Court at First Instance:

This case is a dispute over infringement of a new plant variety right. Based on the parties' allegations and the facts of the case, the issues in dispute are: 1. Whether Defendant Zhang Yang's act of propagating the rice seeds in question infringes the "Longke 638S" new plant variety right claimed by Plaintiff Yahua Institute; 2. If infringement is established, what liability Zhang Yang should bear.

1. Whether Defendant Zhang Yang's act of propagating the rice seeds in question infringes the "Longke 638S" new plant variety right

The "Longke 638S" new plant variety right owned by Plaintiff Yahua Institute shall be protected according to law. Article 28 of the Seed Law provides that a unit or individual that completes a breeding project shall have the exclusive right to its authorized variety. No unit or individual may, without the permission of the owner of the new plant variety right, produce, propagate, or sell the propagating material of the authorized variety, nor may it, for commercial purposes, repeatedly use the propagating material of the authorized variety for producing the propagating material of another variety, unless otherwise provided in this Law, relevant laws, or administrative regulations. Article 6 of the Plant Variety Protection Regulations contains similar provisions. Article 2, Paragraph 1 of the *Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights* stipulates: "Without the permission of the variety right holder, producing, propagating, or selling the propagating material of the authorized variety, or for commercial purposes repeatedly using the propagating material of the authorized variety for producing the propagating material of another variety, shall be determined by the People's Court as infringement of the new plant variety right." Paragraph 3 stipulates: "Where the accused infringer repeatedly uses the propagating material of the authorized variety as a parent stock to propagate separately with other parent stocks, the People's Court shall generally determine that this constitutes, for commercial purposes, the repeated use of the propagating material of the authorized variety for producing the propagating material of another variety."

In this case, upon investigation by the administrative authority and as evidenced by the Inspection Report from the Hangzhou Sub-Center of the Ministry of Agriculture's New Plant Variety Testing Center, the rice seeds propagated by Defendant Zhang Yang in Yazhou District, Sanya, were compared with "Liangyou 1377" over 48 locus points, with zero difference points. The conclusion "very similar variety or identical variety" indicates that the rice variety Zhang Yang propagated was "Liangyou 1377." Since "Liangyou 1377" is a hybrid rice variety bred from two parent stocks (a male parent and a female parent), the major crop variety certificate for "Liangyou 1377" shows that its variety source is "Longke 638S" × "R1377," i.e., "Liangyou 1377" is a hybrid rice variety bred by combining the female parent "Longke 638S" and the male parent "R1377." On June 15, 2020, the Hangzhou Sub-Center of the Ministry of Agriculture's New Plant Variety Testing Center issued an Identification Report proving that the Center compared the unknown variety (in fact, Zhang Yang's propagated variety) with "Longke 638S" using SSR markers with reference to the standard *Technical Procedure for Rice Variety Identification – SSR Marker Method* (NY/T1433-2014) using capillary electrophoresis fluorescence detection. Twenty seeds were randomly selected, germinated, and mixed for DNA extraction, replicated twice. The result was: "Among the 48 SSR markers used, the unknown variety showed homozygous genotypes at 22 markers and heterozygous genotypes at the remaining 26 markers. The sample Longke 638S showed homozygous genotypes at all 48 markers, and one of its genotypes matched one genotype of the unknown variety." The conclusion stated: "The submitted sample and Longke 638S have a genetic relationship."

Regarding Plant Genetic Relationships: The appraisal conclusion that "the submitted sample has a genetic relationship with Longke 638S" does not directly establish that the涉案 rice seeds were bred by crossing the female parent "Longke 638S" with the male parent "R1377." Theoretically, the possibility remains that sister lines of the female and male parents could have been the parents. However, from a practical production perspective, the probability of producing progeny with extremely similar or identical genotypes using different hybrid parent combinations is very low. Therefore, it is highly probable that the涉案 rice seeds were bred using "Longke 638S" as the parent. In this case, based on the appraisal report and identification report submitted by the plaintiff, Yahua Research Institute, if the defendant, Zhang Yangru, contends that the variety he propagated did not originate from "Longke 638S," he must provide evidence that his variety originated from other parents. Zhang Yang failed to adduce evidence that he did not use "Longke 638S." Applying the standard of proof of high probability, the court finds that Zhang Yang engaged in the act of using the protected variety "Longke 638S" to breed "Longliangyou 1377."

Defendant Zhang Yang's Defense: The defendant argued that his breeding activities constituted self-propagation and self-use by a farmer, were not for commercial purposes, and did not constitute repeated use. First, Article 10 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties provides that farmers may, without the permission of the variety rights holder and without paying royalties, use the propagating material of an authorized variety for self-propagation and self-use, provided they do not infringe upon other rights enjoyed by the variety rights holder under these Regulations. Whether an act constitutes self-propagation and self-use by a farmer should be determined by comprehensively considering factors such as the purpose, scale, and profitability of the alleged infringing activity. Furthermore, the farmer must conduct such activities within the scope of land stipulated in their family rural land contract management agreement. In this case, Zhang Yang is a resident of Pingxiang City, Jiangxi Province. He did not provide evidence of his family's contracted land, nor could he reasonably explain how he produced up to 10,000 jin of "Longliangyou 1377" seeds in Sanya using the authorized variety "Longke 638S." Considering Zhang Yang's personal health and family circumstances, producing over 10,000 jin of seeds exceeded a reasonable quantity. Therefore, his breeding activities cannot be deemed self-propagation and self-use by a farmer, nor can the possibility of a commercial purpose be excluded. Second, the term "repeated use" in Article 28 of the Seeds Law should not be simply understood as the number of times an act occurs. Instead, it should be understood as the act of using the propagating material of an authorized variety as a parent to propagate separately with other parents in hybrid rice breeding. Specifically in this case, it refers to the hybrid breeding act of using the female parent "Longke 638S" to propagate the涉案 rice seeds "Longliangyou 1377." Therefore, Zhang Yang's argument during trial that he only used the propagating material of "Longke 638S" (as claimed by the plaintiff, Yahua Research Institute) for a single production and thus did not constitute repeated use is untenable. In summary, Zhang Yang's act of using the authorized variety "Longke 638S" to breed "Longliangyou 1377" seeds without the permission of the variety rights holder, Yahua Research Institute, violates Article 28 of the Seeds Law, Article 6 of the Regulations on the Protection of New Plant Varieties, and Paragraphs 1 and 3 of Article 2 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights, thereby constituting infringement of the new plant variety right for "Longke 638S" claimed by Yahua Research Institute.

II. How the Defendant, Zhang Yang, Should Bear Tort Liability

Article 73, Paragraphs 3 and 4 of the Seeds Law stipulate: "The amount of damages for infringement of new plant variety rights shall be determined based on the actual losses suffered by the right holder due to the infringement; if the actual losses are difficult to determine, it may be determined based on the benefits gained by the infringer from the infringement. If the losses of the right holder or the benefits gained by the infringer are difficult to determine, it may be reasonably determined by reference to a multiple of the reasonable royalty for licensing the use of the new plant variety. The amount of damages shall include the reasonable expenses incurred by the right holder to stop the infringement. Where the infringement of new plant variety rights is of a serious nature, the amount of damages may be determined within the range of one to three times the amount determined according to the above methods. If the losses of the right holder, the benefits gained by the infringer, and the reasonable royalty for licensing the use of the new plant variety are all difficult to determine, the People's Court may, based on factors such as the type of the new plant variety right and the nature and circumstances of the infringement, determine damages of no more than three million yuan." The defendant Zhang Yang's act of using the authorized variety "Longke 638S" to breed "Longliangyou 1377" seeds without permission occurred in May 2020 and was seasonal. His conduct should be governed by the laws and judicial interpretations in force at that time. Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights (before the amendment on December 29, 2020) also stipulates that where infringement is established, the infringer shall bear civil liability such as cessation of infringement and compensation for losses.

The defendant Zhang Yang's act of breeding the涉案 rice seeds infringed the new plant variety right for "Longke 638S" claimed by the plaintiff, Yahua Research Institute. Pursuant to the above laws and judicial interpretations, the court supports Yahua Research Institute's request for an order that Zhang Yang immediately cease infringing its new plant variety right. Additionally, Yahua Research Institute requested the destruction of all infringing seed products and all parent "Longke 638S" seeds. Zhang Yang stated that the涉案 rice seeds he bred were produced over a year ago, have all become moldy and sprouted, are no longer plantable, and have been used to feed chickens and ducks. Yahua Research Institute also failed to provide evidence proving the actual whereabouts of the alleged infringing seed products and parent "Longke 638S" seeds. Therefore, the court does not support Yahua Research Institute's related claims. If Yahua Research Institute later discovers the actual whereabouts of the涉案 infringing seed products and all parent "Longke 638S" seeds, it may file an application with the court, requesting an order for Zhang Yang to destroy the viability of such infringing seed products and all parent "Longke 638S" seeds so that they can no longer be used as propagating material.

Regarding the quantity of infringing seeds and the losses in this case: The plaintiff, Yahua Research Institute, claimed that the damage caused by the defendant Zhang Yang using "Longke 638S" to breed 35,120 jin of "Longliangyou 1377" seeds amounted to approximately 770,000 yuan. This estimate was primarily based on the average sales price and breeding costs of "Longliangyou 1377" seeds from its affiliated company, and assumed a three-year average profit margin of 52% for the affiliated company, yielding an estimated profit from the涉案 rice seeds of about 600,000 yuan. Since it was impossible to accurately calculate Zhang Yang's profit or Yahua Research Institute's own loss, and considering the nature of Zhang Yang's production of the涉案 rice seeds, the approximate profit range, and the actual expenses incurred in enforcing rights, the court was requested to award damages of 500,000 yuan to Yahua Research Institute based on statutory damages. Zhang Yang argued in response that after thorough drying, de-stemming, winnowing, and other selection procedures, the actual breeding weight was 26,000 jin, and the figure of 35,120 jin was an estimate. He further claimed that during questioning by administrative enforcement officers, the seeds were not actually weighed, and being disabled, he was not in a position to consider or confirm the actual weight when signing the interview record. The court opined that since the new plant variety sought to be protected in this case is "Longke 638S," the losses or infringer's gains are not directly determined based on the quantity of "Longliangyou 1377" produced or sold. Therefore, whether Zhang Yang bred 35,120 jin or 26,000 jin of "Longliangyou 1377" seeds does not affect the court's determination of the compensation amount based on the specific circumstances of this case.

The defendant Zhang Yang repeatedly used the propagating material of the authorized variety "Longke 638S" to produce propagating material of another variety, "Longliangyou 1377." However, the plaintiff, Yahua Research Institute, did not provide specific information on the licensing fee for the use of the parent "Longke 638S" variety for reference. Furthermore, it was impossible to accurately deduce the price of the "Longke 638S" variety from the average purchase and sales prices of the "Longliangyou 1377" variety licensed for production and sale by its affiliated company, as claimed and provided by Yahua Research Institute. Consequently, the actual losses for this part and the licensing fee for the "Longke 638S" variety could not be determined. The profits gained by Zhang Yang were also difficult to ascertain. Taking into comprehensive consideration factors such as the type of the涉案 new plant variety right, the nature and circumstances of the infringement, and the reasonable expenses incurred by Yahua Research Institute in stopping the infringement, and with reference to the circumstances under which Yahua Research Institute licensed its affiliated company to produce and sell the "Longliangyou 1377" variety, the court, in its discretion, determines that Zhang Yang's compensation amount, including reasonable expenses of 35,000 yuan, totals 100,000 yuan.

The defendant Zhang Yang argued that he had no subjective intent to infringe, that he ceased the subsequent breeding activities upon learning that they might infringe upon others' rights, that he cooperated with administrative enforcement officers, that he did not sell or sow the seeds, that the infringement was negligent and did not cause serious consequences, and requested exemption from liability for damages. The court opined that Article 8 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights stipulates: "An individual who makes a living from agriculture or forestry, or a rural contracted household, who accepts another person's commission to propagate material that infringes variety rights, and who did not know that the material being propagated on commission was material infringing variety rights and identifies the principal, shall not bear liability for damages." In this case, Zhang Yang used all the parents he purchased to breed the "Longliangyou 1377" seed product. He could not provide the legal source of the purchased seeds, nor did he prove that he propagated them on commission from another person. Therefore, he does not meet the conditions for exemption from liability for damages.

In conclusion, the defendant Zhang Yang's actions constitute infringement of the plaintiff Yahua Research Institute's new plant variety right for "Longke 638S." Some of Yahua Research Institute's claims are established. The Hainan Free Trade Port Intellectual Property Court, pursuant to Article 28 and Article 73, Paragraph 4 of the Seeds Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 6 and Article 39 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of New Plant Varieties, and Article 2, Paragraphs 1 and 3, and Article 6 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Specific Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Infringement of New Plant Variety Rights, on October 8, 2021, rendered the following judgment:

1. The defendant, Zhang Yang, shall immediately cease infringing the plaintiff, Hunan Yahua Seed Industry Science Research Institute's, new plant variety right for "Longke 638S";
2. The defendant, Zhang Yang, shall, within ten days of the effective date of this judgment, pay the plaintiff, Hunan Yahua Seed Industry Science Research Institute, economic losses including reasonable expenses totaling 100,000 yuan;
3. The remaining claims of the plaintiff, Hunan Yahua Seed Industry Science Research Institute, are dismissed.

Following the pronouncement of the first-instance judgment, neither party filed an appeal. The first-instance judgment has become legally effective.
